title: Ch 13 Test (GSEB pattern): Our Environment
subject: Science
instructions: Section A: objective questions, 1 mark each. Section B: 2 marks each. Section C: 3 marks each. Section D: 4 marks.
Write balanced equations and draw neat, labelled diagrams wherever needed.

questions.q: Which group contains only biodegradable items?
options: Fruit peels, cake and lime juice
questions.answer: (b) Fruit peels, cake and lime juice

questions.q: Which of the following is an artificial ecosystem?
Which of the following forms a food chain?

options: Switching off unnecessary lights and fans
Walking to school instead of being dropped by scooter

questions.q: In the food chain grass → deer → tiger, the tiger is a:
In a food chain, the energy passed on to the next trophic level is about:
options: the same as the previous level
questions.answer: (b) 10% of the previous level (10 per cent law)

questions.q: Which of these is a good way to manage household waste?
Depletion of the ozone layer is mainly caused by:
What are decomposers? What would happen if there were no decomposers?
questions.answer: Decomposers are micro-organisms, such as bacteria and fungi, that break down the dead remains and waste products of organisms into simpler substances. Without them, dead bodies and wastes would pile up, and nutrients would not be returned to the soil for plants to use.

questions.q: What will happen if all the organisms in one trophic level are killed?
questions.answer: The food chain will break. Organisms of the next trophic level will lose their food and may starve or die out, while the population of the level below may increase greatly. This upsets the balance of the ecosystem.

questions.q: What is biological magnification? Why is it highest in organisms at the top of a food chain?
questions.answer: The progressive build-up of non-biodegradable chemicals, such as pesticides, at each trophic level of a food chain. Organisms at the top eat many organisms from the levels below, and these chemicals are not broken down, so the concentration keeps increasing up the chain.

questions.q: Study the food chain: Grass → Grasshopper → Frog → Snake → Eagle

subparts.q: Identify the producer and the tertiary consumer.
If 10,000 J of energy is available at the producer level, how much energy will reach the snake?
Which organism will have the highest concentration of a pesticide that enters this food chain? Why?
subparts.answer: The eagle. It is at the top of the food chain, and pesticides build up at each level (biological magnification).

questions.q: Study the pond food chain: phytoplankton → zooplankton → small fish → big fish

subparts.q: At which trophic level is the small fish?
If the phytoplankton capture 50,000 J of energy, how much energy is available to the big fish?
Why are there far fewer big fish than small fish in the pond?
subparts.answer: Much less energy is available at the higher trophic level, so it can support fewer organisms.

sections.title: Section D
sections.note: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

questions.q: Some years ago, it was proposed that tea on trains should be served in disposable kulhads (clay cups) instead of plastic cups. It was soon realised that making kulhads on such a large scale would cause the loss of fertile top soil. Now, disposable paper cups are commonly used.

subparts.q: Why was it proposed to replace plastic cups?
subparts.answer: Plastic is non-biodegradable and pollutes the environment.

subparts.q: What was the problem with using kulhads on a large scale?
Give one advantage of paper cups over plastic cups and one over kulhads.
subparts.answer: Over plastic: paper is biodegradable (and can be recycled). Over kulhads: making paper cups does not use up fertile top soil.
